steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals

steps.finding: 31 inspections (2 OAI at our plants), 2 compliance actions, 0 import-alert listings, 0 recalls.

steps.title: What FDA wrote at the OAI inspections
steps.purpose: Read the Form 483 observations recorded at those inspections.

steps.title: What our P&T committee already approved
steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.title: Which links can't be trusted
steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

explanation.headline: FDA's records trace our supply to a plant classified OAI 623 days before the 2018 shortage posting

sentences.text: Diltiazem hydrochloride is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21; FDA's history shows an earlier shortage first posted on 2018-02-21, since resolved.
FDA inspection 976095 at Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) ended 2016-06-08 and was classified OAI, 623 days before the 2018-02-21 shortage posting.
A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2017-02-14, 372 days before the shortage posting.
A later FDA inspection 1064827 at the plant ended 2018-08-15 and was classified OAI, 175 days after the shortage posting.

rejected.text: The 2018 shortage posting listed Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer Company, with status To Be Discontinued for package NDC 0409-4350-03.
rejected.reason: number 2018 is not in the cited evidence

rejected.text: Our 100 mg injection vials at both Corvale General and Corvale East carry NDC 00409435003 and labeler Hospira, Inc., matching the discontinued product.
rejected.reason: status claim ("discontinued") that the cited record does not make

rejected.text: The rule-based best option is to transfer 50 vials of 100 mg from Corvale General to Corvale East, which would raise Corvale East from 9.3 to 14 days on hand while Corvale General remains above two weeks.
rejected.reason: "two" is a number in words; numbers must be digits from the evidence

memory.text: Decision on carboplatin: move the primary carboplatin contract from Accord to Teva and keep Accord as secondary. Rationale: Accord's supplier plant had an FDA warning letter; Teva supply steadier (demo history). Approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD.

Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.
